clue.text: It helps one hear support for rider

definitions.meaning: one of the three tiny bones of the middle ear, the stapes, carries this name
the metal loop hanging from a saddle in which a horse rider's foot rests

explanation.surface: A puzzle about some object that serves both a listener and a horseman.
explanation.walkthrough: The ear bone (stapes) is named after the riding loop because of its shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: an ear ossicle and the footrest hung from a saddle share the name.

clue.text: Mother's in Slough getting drunk

indicators.note: in places the mother inside the other word

parts.note: to slough a skin is to shed it
Ma's, mother's in its short form

explanation.surface: Mum getting plastered in the Berkshire town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slough' looks like the town west of London; here it is the verb meaning to cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashed is informal slang for very intoxicated.

clue.text: During school time, keeping current caretaker

parts.note: in, as in 'in the summer', means during

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside

parts.note: a school term is a period of time
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A school caretaker holding on to electricity during term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caretaker' looks like the school janitor but is an adjective, as in a caretaker government.
explanation.definitionFit: A caretaker government is a temporary one holding office until a successor arrives, so provisional.

clue.text: One's endangered removing designer drug from highborn rogue

indicators.note: rogue means behaving wildly, so the letters are rearranged
removing means taking letters out

parts.note: GHB is a synthetic club drug

explanation.surface: A rogue aristocrat stripped of his party drugs is in danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rogue' looks like a noun for the aristocrat but signals rearranging HIORN, left once GHB goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Several species of the horned African and Asian beast are critically threatened by poaching.

clue.text: Sail open at sea, going round unknown islands

indicators.note: going round means surrounding the other letter
at sea means confused, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Setting sail on the open ocean, circling uncharted islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The region is a large group of Pacific island chains such as Hawaii and Samoa.

clue.text: Go-between closed Brexit deal finally with European

parts.note: closed means shut

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of each of the words Brexit and deal

explanation.surface: A diplomatic go-between sealing the final Brexit agreement with Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Shuttle diplomacy: something that travels back and forth between two parties acts as an intermediary.

clue.text: Instrument without charge, no good getting upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read backwards
no signals the letter for good is left out

parts.note: gratis means free of charge

explanation.surface: A musical instrument handed over free and found to be no good, causing upset.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a long-necked Indian stringed instrument that is plucked.

clue.text: Due no ill with firm wearing proscribed attire

indicators.note: ill means badly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A firm with no obligation to its staff, fussing over banned clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill' looks like part of the fodder but signals rearranging DUE NO with FIRM.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dressed in the set official outfit, as soldiers or police are, means being in uniform.

clue.text: Regularly dismissed Tardis, container that's unimportant

indicators.note: every other letter of the word Tardis is dropped, keeping the odd ones

parts.note: a vial is a small container

explanation.surface: Doctor Who's Tardis written off as just a box of no consequence.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tardis is the police-box time machine in the BBC series Doctor Who.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trivial is slight and of little consequence.

clue.text: Most irritable from bananas not fully digested

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters are rearranged
not fully means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Feeling crabby after eating bananas that have not been properly digested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like fruit but means mad; it rearranges DIGESTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy means tense and nervous, so its superlative is the most on edge.

clue.text: Time invested in renovated hall in colonial residence

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, as money is put into something
renovated means done up and reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Money and time spent restoring a hall within some old colonial home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'colonial' points to imperial history, but the colony here is one of ants.
explanation.definitionFit: An ant colony lives in a mound of earth it builds, so that mound is the colony's home.

clue.text: Cat skipping about, poorly stalking

indicators.note: skipping means leaving out, so the letters for about are dropped from the word cat

parts.note: CA (circa) is the abbreviation for about
poorly means unwell, ailing

explanation.surface: A sick cat hopping about while it hunts its prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cat' looks like the definition but loses CA (circa, about) to leave just T.
explanation.definitionFit: To tail someone is to follow them secretly, which is the same as stalking.

clue.text: Crew member prepared to shoot comedian with single take

parts.note: Harpo Marx, the silent comedian of the Marx Brothers
single means one
R stands for recipe, Latin for take, as on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A film crew member ready to shoot a comic actor in a single take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoot' and 'take' suggest filming; the crew is a whaling ship's and the shooting is with a harpoon.
explanation.definitionFit: On a whaler, the sailor who fires or throws the barbed spear is ready to shoot at the quarry.

clue.text: Nothing bad about fruit

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing

indicators.note: about signals turning the following word round

parts.note: bad means evil

explanation.surface: A shrug that there is nothing wrong with the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The small oily stone fruit of a Mediterranean tree is a fruit.

clue.text: One filmed flying doctor with pair outside

indicators.note: outside says the pair surrounds the doctor

parts.note: a pair is a duo
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A flying doctor travelling with two others round him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying doctor' reads as one phrase but splits: the flying belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Disney's 1941 film features a baby elephant who flies using his huge ears.

clue.text: Cook — he's done it as an extra job

indicators.note: to cook is to doctor or rearrange, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A cook boasting that he's done some moonlighting work.
explanation.definitionFit: Work done on the side is extra employment besides one's main job.

clue.text: Small toes transmogrified in horror story

indicators.note: transmogrified means transformed bizarrely, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Little toes grotesquely transformed, like something from a horror tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen King's vampire novel about a Maine town is a famous horror story.

clue.text: Feeling of torpor from drink daughter consumed in day

parts.note: lassi is an Indian yogurt drink

indicators.note: consumed in means swallowed inside

parts.note: TUE is the abbreviation for Tuesday

explanation.surface: Sluggishness from a drink a daughter downed during the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude is physical or mental weariness, a sense of lethargy.

clue.text: Money to acquire net pieces of underwear

indicators.note: to acquire means to take in, so one word holds the other

parts.note: brass is slang for money
a net is a trap

explanation.surface: Spending money to buy net lingerie.
explanation.definitionFit: The shoulder bands holding up a brassiere are parts of underwear.

clue.text: "Cap's second rate" — I upset Cockney milliner

parts.note: B grade means second rate

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: a hatter with the H dropped, as Cockneys do, is 'atter

explanation.surface: A Cockney hatmaker grumbles that his cap is second rate.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the London working-class accent, which drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: A biretta is a square cap with ridges worn by Catholic clergy.

clue.text: Practical computer program was misleading

parts.note: an app is a computer program
lied means was misleading

explanation.surface: A useful bit of software that turned out to deceive.
explanation.definitionFit: Applied science is put to practical use rather than being theoretical.

clue.text: Mass of timber rejected in practical lesson

indicators.note: in places the reversed timber inside the lesson

parts.note: DT is Design and Technology, a hands-on school subject in Britain

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: fir is a timber

explanation.surface: A heap of wood discarded during a hands-on class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass of timber' looks like one phrase but 'Mass' alone is the definition. DT (Design and Technology) is a British school workshop subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A drift is a heap of material piled up by wind or water, as in snowdrift.

clue.text: Heinous criminal using company's assets

indicators.note: criminal means wrong or bent, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wicked crook misusing corporate resources.
explanation.definitionFit: Work done internally relies on the firm's own staff and resources rather than outside contractors.

clue.text: Betrays Swiss marksman at location of intended target

definitions.text: Swiss marksman at location of intended target
definitions.meaning: William Tell shot an apple off his son's head, so the Swiss hero's aim was at his boy

explanation.surface: A Swiss sharpshooter turns traitor at the target site.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as TELL + SON: Tell's target sat on his son.
explanation.definitionFit: Grassing someone up means reporting their wrongdoing, betraying them; the legend gives the other sense.

clue.text: Recipe amiss, ghee should be halved to make Indian bread

parts.note: something amiss is up, as in what's up?

indicators.note: halved keeps only one half, here the back half of the word ghee

explanation.surface: Cooking advice: a botched recipe needs half the ghee for Indian flatbread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' is slang for money, so Indian bread is the currency, not a naan.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, and the Indian unit of currency is cash from India.

clue.text: Jubilant to bag Romeo, ham it up playing line

indicators.note: to bag means to capture, so the anagram holds the letter
playing means performing loosely, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An actor overplays a line, thrilled to land the role of Romeo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges HAM IT UP; 'to bag' sets R inside that, and L follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Something triumphal celebrates a victory, so it is exultant and joyful.

clue.text: Capers and offal, seconds for European

indicators.note: for signals one letter replacing another

parts.note: tripe is offal, a cow's stomach lining

explanation.surface: A menu of capers and offal, with second helpings for a European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capers' looks like the pickled buds on the menu; it means jaunts.
explanation.definitionFit: Capers and outings are both lighthearted jaunts or excursions.

clue.text: Head down in cramped places busy at Christmas

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first letter moves down to the bottom

parts.note: cramped means small

explanation.surface: Keeping one's head down in crowded festive shopping.
explanation.definitionFit: Shopping centres are crowded with gift buyers in the run-up to the holidays.

clue.text: Georgian place is bit special, astride island on lake

indicators.note: astride means straddling, so the anagram sits either side of the other letters
special treatment here means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rather special Georgian spot straddling an island in a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Georgian' suggests 18th-century English architecture; it means the country Georgia. 'on' sets I before L.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital city of the Caucasian republic of Georgia.

clue.text: German Marks I'm not sure you heard to be among last in circulation

parts.note: um is a hesitant sound of uncertainty

indicators.note: to be among means to sit inside, so one piece goes into the other
in circulation means moving around, so the letters are shuffled
heard says the word is said aloud and spelt as the letter that sounds the same

parts.note: you sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: Uncertainty over whether old Deutschmarks are still being circulated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German Marks' suggests the old currency but means the two-dot accents. 'in circulation' rearranges LAST to LATS, and U goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The two dots over a vowel in German writing are diacritic signs, the marks themselves.

clue.text: Attend to details of one's home

definitions.meaning: to deal with or tackle a problem
the house number, street and town where one lives

explanation.surface: Someone told to deal with the particulars of their house.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a verb for dealing with a matter, the other the location written on letters.

clue.text: A novelist cycled from Asia, perhaps

indicators.note: cycled means the last letter goes round to the front

parts.note: Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy

explanation.surface: A writer who travelled by bicycle on an Asian journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycled' moves the final E of A STERNE to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia lies to the east, so something from there is oriental; 'perhaps' marks Asia as one example.
